indication_label: US label: adults with hemophilia B on FIX prophylaxis, or with current/historical life-threatening bleeding, or repeated serious spontaneous bleeds
verbatim: HEMGENIX, etranacogene dezaparvovec-drlb, is a one-time gene therapy for the treatment of adults with hemophilia B who: Currently use Factor IX prophylaxis therapy, or Have current or historical life-threatening bleeding, or Have repeated, serious spontaneous bleeding episodes.
source_doc: CSL Behring press release, First Patient Has Received FDA-Approved HEMGENIX (2023-06-20)
notes: FDA approval 2022-11-22. US label has no AAV5-antibody or FIX-inhibitor exclusion in the indication statement (inhibitor testing is in the warnings). Registered trademark symbol dropped from quote.

indication_label: EU label: severe and moderately severe haemophilia B, adults without history of FIX inhibitors
verbatim: Hemgenix ist indiziert zur Behandlung von schwerer und mittelschwerer Haemophilie B (angeborener Faktor-IX-Mangel) bei erwachsenen Patienten ohne Faktor-IX-Inhibitoren in ihrer Vorgeschichte.
source_doc: G-BA Beschluss Anlage XII Etranacogen Dezaparvovec (Haemophilie B), Beschluss vom 19. Oktober 2023, BAnz AT 24.11.2023 B4, section 2 Anzahl der Patientinnen und Patienten
notes: EU authorisation 2023-02-20 (Anwendungsgebiet laut Zulassung). SmPC adds that pre-existing anti-AAV5 neutralising antibody titre above 1:678 may reduce efficacy (per HAS summary), not an indication exclusion. Umlauts transliterated.

indication_label: adult severe hemophilia B without inhibitors (ICER budget-impact population)
verbatim: For PBIA 1, using Centers for Disease Control (CDC) data and other sources, we estimated that approximately 860 adult severe hemophilia B patients without inhibitors would be eligible for treatment with etranacogene dezaparvovec. This equates to approximately 172 patients being treated per year over 5 years when assuming 20% of all eligible patients are treated each year.
source_doc: ICER, Gene Therapy for Hemophilia B and An Update on Gene Therapy for Hemophilia A: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report (posted 2022-12-22, unmasked 2024-07-26), section 7 (report p.38) and Appendix F (p.F1)
notes: Derivation (Appendix F): US population ~342,000,000 x 49.5% male x CDC age-adjusted prevalence of hemophilia B 0.0037% x 52.8% adults x 28.7% severe x 90.9% without inhibitors. Counts only severe (FIX <1%); moderately severe patients on prophylaxis, who are in the label, are excluded, so this is a lower bound of the label pool. No AAV5-seropositivity exclusion applied. 20%/yr uptake assumption = ~172 treated/yr.

source_doc: EMA orphan designation page EU/3/19/2210 (exagamglogene autotemcel, beta thalassaemia)
notes: Includes non-transfusion-dependent intermedia; TDT 12+ HSCT-eligible without donor is a fraction.

indication_label: CDEC reimbursement criteria (TDT 12+, transfusions of at least 100 mL/kg/yr or 10 units/yr for 2 years, autologous-transplant eligible, no willing 10/10 HLA-matched related donor)
verbatim: Casgevy should only be covered to treat patients 12 years of age and older with a diagnosis of TDT (defined as documented homozygous or compound heterozygous beta-thalassemia, and having received transfusions of packed red blood cells [RBCs] of at least 100mL/kg/year, or 10 units/year, during the previous 2 years)
source_doc: CDA-AMC Reimbursement Recommendation, Exagamglogene Autotemcel (Casgevy) for TDT, NCBI Bookshelf NBK612160 (2025)
notes: Counts not stated in summary; CDA-AMC reanalysis budget impact $64,614,557 over 3 years (year 1 $3,052,191; year 2 $18,400,764; year 3 $43,161,602).

indication_label: people living with TDT in the US (ICER)
verbatim: There are likely between 1,000 - 1,500 people in the US living with TDT,1,2 but there are estimated to be about 1.25 million carriers of the genetic defect that is responsible for thalassemia.
source_doc: ICER, Betibeglogene Autotemcel for Beta Thalassemia: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report (2022-07-19), Executive Summary
notes: US label for Zynteglo (FDA 2022-08-17) covers adults and children with TDT, all genotypes, so this prevalent pool is close to the label pool before HSCT-fitness screening.

indication_label: individuals aged 0-50 with TDT eligible for beti-cel (ICER budget-impact population)
verbatim: This budget impact analysis included the estimated number of individuals ages 0 to 50 years with TDT in the US who would be eligible for treatment with beti-cel. Using this approach, we derived an estimate of 666 patients in the US eligible for treatment with beti-cel. Our estimate begins with prevalent cases of beta thalassemia in the US of roughly 2,100.48 From there, we assumed that about 63% of patients could be classified as having TDT arriving at approximately 1,333 patients.2 Of patients who are diagnosed with transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia, we assumed that 50% would be eligible for treatment with beti-cel, arriving at approximately 666 patients.
source_doc: ICER, Betibeglogene Autotemcel for Beta Thalassemia: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report (2022-07-19), section 7.1 (report p.63) and Supplement F
notes: 20%/yr uptake assumption = ~133 treated per year. Supplement F uses incidence 1 in 100,000 applied to the US population aged 2-50 and TDT share 63.0%.

indication_label: TDT worldwide vs US (ICER policy section)
verbatim: Policy-makers and life science companies should consider that there are 300,000 people living with transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia (TDT) worldwide, but only 1,000 of them reside in the US.
source_doc: ICER, Betibeglogene Autotemcel for Beta Thalassemia: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report (2022-07-19)
notes: Gives a US point estimate of 1,000 alongside the 1,000-1,500 range.

source_doc: bluebird bio, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year ended 2024-12-31 (filed 2025)

indication_label: US label: patients aged 6 months and older and adults with WAS (WAS gene mutation) for whom HSCT is appropriate and no suitable HLA-matched related donor is available
verbatim: Waskyra is an autologous hematopoietic stem cell-based gene therapy indicated for the treatment of pediatric patients aged 6 months and older and adults with Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome (WAS) who have a mutation in the WAS gene for whom hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is appropriate and no suitable human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-matched related stem cell donor is available.
source_doc: Fondazione Telethon press release, FDA approval of Waskyra (etuvetidigene autotemcel) (2025-12-10)
notes: FDA approval 2025-12-09 (first approval to a non-profit applicant). Label is not restricted to severe WAS (classic phenotype), but HSCT-appropriateness in practice limits use to patients for whom transplant is indicated. Not approved in the EU as of this record.

indication_label: WAS birth incidence (company statement)

source_doc: Fondazione Telethon press release, FDA approval of Waskyra (etuvetidigene autotemcel) (2025-12-10)
notes: Rate only. Equivalent to 4 per million male births.

notes: Orphanet page (ORPHA:906) could not be read (anti-bot verification page).

indication_label: births with WAS per year (annual incident flow)

notes: ASSUMPTION not fetched: ~3.6 million US births per year, ~51% male (~1.84 million male births). Using the MedlinePlus range 1-10 per million males gives ~2-18 per year. Prevalent pool without a matched related donor (about 70-75% of patients) and not already transplanted was not found.

indication_label: EU label: ADA-SCID patients with no suitable HLA-matched related stem cell donor
verbatim: Strimvelis is indicated for the treatment of patients with severe combined immunodeficiency due to adenosine deaminase deficiency (ADA-SCID), for whom no suitable human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-matched related stem cell donor is available
source_doc: EMA, Strimvelis EPAR page and EPAR summary for the public (authorised 2016-05-26)
notes: Administered only at Ospedale San Raffaele, Milan. EPAR summary: 'Because the number of patients with ADA-SCID is low, the disease is considered rare, and Strimvelis was designated an orphan medicine ... on 26 August 2005.' Main study involved 12 patients aged 6 months to about 6 years.

indication_label: all SCD, Canada excluding Quebec (sponsor prevalence model)
verbatim: First, the sponsor estimates that there are 4,391 patients in Canada (excluding Quebec) who have SCD, using a model informed by literature-derived prevalence, primary market research, and province-specific race- and ethnicity-based demographic data, which was then applied to province-specific demographic data to estimate the overall prevalence of SCD in CDA-AMC-participating jurisdictions.
source_doc: CDA-AMC Pharmacoeconomic Review, Exagamglogene Autotemcel (Casgevy) for sickle cell disease with recurrent VOCs, NCBI Bookshelf NBK614941 (2025)
notes: Disease-level base for CDA-AMC-participating drug plans (Quebec excluded). Eligible subset (12+, at least 2 VOCs/yr, fit for myeloablation) derived from proxy US/European inputs (Bionest market research).

indication_label: patients 12+ with SCD and recurrent VOCs eligible for exa-cel (implied sponsor pool)
verbatim: (derived) 6 patients at 0.5% market share = ~1,200; 21 patients at 1.9% = ~1,105
source_doc: CDA-AMC Pharmacoeconomic Review, Exagamglogene Autotemcel (Casgevy) for sickle cell disease with recurrent VOCs, NCBI Bookshelf NBK614941 (2025) (derived)
notes: Sponsor text: 'the anticipated market share of exagamglogene autotemcel for SCD was assumed to be 0% in Year 1, 0.5% in Year 2, and 1.9% in Year 3, resulting in 0, 6, and 21 patients receiving exagamglogene autotemcel in each year, respectively.' Market share is applied to the eligible target population, so eligible = patients / share. CDA-AMC scenario 'aligned with expert input obtained by the sponsor': 23, 47 and 65 patients treated in years 1-3. Sponsor 3-year budget impact $59,337,641; CDA-AMC reanalysis $59,373,150.

indication_label: patients treated per year with exa-cel for SCD (sponsor base case vs expert scenario)
verbatim: the anticipated market share of exagamglogene autotemcel for SCD was assumed to be 0% in Year 1, 0.5% in Year 2, and 1.9% in Year 3, resulting in 0, 6, and 21 patients receiving exagamglogene autotemcel in each year, respectively. | Assuming that more patients will receive exagamglogene autotemcel (23 patients in year 1, 47 patients in year 2, and 65 patients in year 3), aligned with expert input obtained by the sponsor.
source_doc: CDA-AMC Pharmacoeconomic Review, Exagamglogene Autotemcel (Casgevy) for sickle cell disease with recurrent VOCs, NCBI Bookshelf NBK614941 (2025)
notes: Uptake benchmark, not eligibility. Two sentences joined with |.

indication_label: patients 12+ with TDT treated per year with exa-cel (implied from sponsor budget impact at $2.8M per administration)
source_doc: CDA-AMC Pharmacoeconomic Review, Exagamglogene Autotemcel (Casgevy) for transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia, NCBI Bookshelf NBK616627 (2025) (derived)
notes: Sponsor text: 'The submitted price is $2,800,000 per administration per patient, regardless of the number of patient-specific vials required.' and 'The sponsor estimated the 3-year budget impact of reimbursing exagamglogene autotemcel for the treatment of patients aged 12 years and older with TDT to be $64,585,283 (year 1: $3,052,191; year 2: $18,397,226; year 3: $43,135,865).'
